summary: Protected .github PR4587 delivers this source-only extension. The source ledger extends the accepted PR4584/4585 consumer with separate earlier ACK/read and terminal callback-reader observations. The old eleven-group ledger, all 143 observations, 13 aliases and 8 missing obligations remain prefixes; the extension has 13 separate groups. The original PR1005-backed terminal group remains 11,353 backing-capacity bytes across eleven selected arrays, with six payload-backing aliases and the original-request thirteen/current-request 295 logical-byte alias; payload slices are not allocations. The new PR1007-backed earlier cut holds the third ACK/phase four write before return, child read five waiting for ordinal four, confirmed ordinal two and phase six queued. Actual state/channel/awaiter joins bind 199-byte ACK and 2,048-byte child-read arrays, totaling 2,247 backing-capacity bytes within that cut only. They are mutually distinct and disjoint from eighteen endpoint arrays and the parser input. Twenty classified arrays have explicit classes; parser alias_class stays null because parser-endpoint overlap is unproved, so no twenty-first distinct array or parser capacity is invented. Protected PR1009 supplies a separate terminal callback-reader cut: actual forwarded stdout read memory has complete array capacity one, memory length one and offset zero; its backing aliases the production callback-state buffer. Observer and underlying tasks are distinct/incomplete with exact named bridge/continuation/awaiter joins. The retained reader is incomplete; no additional Task equality is asserted. The one-byte backing is disjoint from eleven selected arrays and 26 endpoints. Those 37 identities are object-count witnesses in this new group: 38 distinct arrays, only one capacity byte recorded. No capacity or identity is imported from the older 11,353 group. The existing grammar suffices; parser source is unchanged. Source pins, roles, aliases, null parser class, ownership and cuts are bound by focused mutation controls; original prefixes have a positive drift control. Scope labels name controlled source witnesses, not authenticated execution IDs. Backing capacity, logical bytes, object counts and physical bounds remain separate; no cross-cut sum, peak, lifetime/reclamation or full physical fit follows. Generic reconciliation checks input consistency, not remote-source authenticity. Runtime/stream/encoding/caller/backend/peer, earlier ACK, failure/restart/uncertainty and physical overhead populations remain unresolved. fit=unproved/admission=false; installed/native/custody/authenticity and original .103 attempted-unknown/unreplayed/.104 hold remain.
